product_requirements.text:
# Product requirements — M0 baseline

## Authority and outcome
The owner brief controls requirements. The 35-page research PDF informs design;
where its compressed roadmap differs, use the explicit 22-milestone owner roadmap.
The goal is a reproducible Python strategy research workflow comparable in function
to MultiCharts/AmiBroker, with independent event execution, accounting and analytics.
Profitability or durable benchmark outperformance is not a software acceptance test.

## Releases and users
- 0.1, M0–8: trusted backtester, data, ledger, orders, analytics, HTML reports and provenance.
- 0.2, M9–14: optimisation, walk-forward, Monte Carlo, robustness, API/CLI and React UI.
- 0.5, M15–18: performance, isolation, realtime paper architecture and one broker boundary.
- 1.0, M19–21: modular advanced research/assets, hardening and release evidence.

Researchers write trusted Python strategies and compare every trial. Traders inspect
fill timing and execution costs. Risk/validation independently challenge results.
Data and engineering roles maintain data and services. Business, legal, audit and
workplace roles inspect role-relevant governance, usability and evidence; they do
not become trading agents merely because the terminal is available.

## Initial supported scope
Equities and ETFs, daily and one-minute completed OHLCV bars; multiple instruments
in one account currency. An explicit exchange calendar and instrument metadata are
mandatory. XNYS/XNAS are initial calendar targets, not a claim of calendar coverage
until validated. Synthetic fixtures are labeled and never presented as market evidence.
Reference accounting supports signed quantities and short fixtures, but deployable
short strategies remain blocked without explicit borrowing/financing assumptions.
Initial backtests use a cash long-only policy unless configured simulation assumptions
explicitly authorise shorts and leverage. No options, full futures, FX conversion,
L2/L3, HFT, production live deployment or multi-broker scope initially.

## Required user workflow
Register immutable dataset → author strategy → specify parameters and financial
assumptions → submit reproducible backtest → inspect orders/fills/positions/trades,
NAV, costs and metrics → export HTML/JSON/CSV/Parquet → rerun and compare → optimise
all trials → freeze selections using IS only → stitch OOS → bootstrap and perturb
assumptions → produce a report showing limitations. Later use unchanged strategy
business logic against a paper broker, with fault/restart/reconciliation tests.

## Acceptance requirements
PR-01 One Strategy lifecycle emits intents, never changes balances.
PR-02 Every fill has an order, timing/model/risk decision and traceable ledger effect.
PR-03 Future or unavailable data is rejected by the data capability boundary.
PR-04 Economic results reproduce with fixed inputs; run identity/time may differ.
PR-05 Golden scenarios independently reconcile NAV and costs; failures block gates.
PR-06 Metrics define formula, annualisation, edge cases and tolerance.
PR-07 All trials/windows/failed experiments are preserved, not only winners.
PR-08 CLI and UI call the same application service contracts.
PR-09 Strategies never receive broker secrets; live operation remains separately gated.
PR-10 All 370 roles have assigned scope, evidence, and later terminal interaction records.
PR-11 Final v1 acceptance executes the complete research lifecycle and a paper parity
demonstration; no release claim before it passes.

## Decisions and limits
No purchased datasets or subscriptions. Benchmark is explicitly none unless a
versioned compatible series is supplied. No automatic liquidation at run end.
The existing ETF desk is a reference artifact only, not an accepted implementation.
No UI polish before the M0–8 financial core. Agent count is not computational parallelism.
Broker environment setup is not a strategy test or permission to transact.

system_architecture.text:
# System architecture

## Architecture decision
Use a Python modular monolith with a deterministic reference event engine. Pure
domain contracts have no dependency on FastAPI, UI, database or broker SDKs.
Application services orchestrate domains; adapters implement storage/data/brokers.
Python 3.12+ is the target; installed 3.13 is a candidate subject to M1 dependency
verification. SQLite metadata, immutable Parquet snapshots and DuckDB analytics
are initial choices. NumPy/SciPy analytics are separate from Decimal accounting.
FastAPI/Pydantic and React/TypeScript/Plotly arrive at M13/M14. No distributed cluster.

## Dependency and ownership boundaries
core → data/strategy/orders/execution/portfolio/risk → engine → analytics →
experiments/reporting/application services → adapters/API/CLI/UI.
Arrows indicate conceptual flow; core imports no higher layer. Analytics consumes
results, never mutable strategy state. Strategy obtains a restricted read capability
and immutable portfolio view, returning intents through its context. Engine alone
coordinates clock, execution, accounting and event sequencing.
One event-loop writer owns an account ledger. Concurrent experiments have separate
run directories and deterministic random streams. API jobs use bounded processes,
not unbounded work on the request loop. Indexes may be rebuilt from immutable records.

## Strategy, execution and portfolio
```mermaid
flowchart LR
 D[Available market event] --> S[Strategy callback]
 S --> I[OrderIntent]
 I --> R[Pre-trade risk]
 R --> B[Historical or paper broker]
 B --> F[Immutable fills]
 F --> L[Portfolio ledger]
 L --> V[Read-only portfolio view]
 V --> S
```

## Historical data
```mermaid
flowchart LR
 CSV[CSV or Parquet input] --> Q[Schema and calendar validation]
 Q --> H[Hash snapshot and metadata]
 H --> P[Immutable Parquet store]
 P --> A[Availability-filtered DataFeed]
 A --> E[Ordered engine events]
```

## Experiment orchestration
```mermaid
flowchart LR
 C[CLI / API / UI] --> M[Canonical manifest]
 M --> J[Bounded job queue]
 J --> W[Isolated run worker]
 W --> E[Event engine]
 E --> O[Immutable artifacts]
 O --> X[Searchable metadata index]
```

## Optimisation
```mermaid
flowchart LR
 S[Seed and search space] --> T[Stable trial IDs]
 T --> B[Backtests with IS-only capability]
 B --> A[All trial results]
 A --> C[Constraint filter and deterministic ranking]
 C --> P[Frozen parameter proposal]
```

## Walk-forward
```mermaid
flowchart LR
 W[Half-open window plan] --> I[IS-only optimiser]
 I --> F[Freeze parameters and selection record]
 F --> O[OOS-only backtest]
 O --> S[Non-overlapping stitched OOS returns]
 S --> R[Window and degradation report]
```

## Monte Carlo
```mermaid
flowchart LR
 R[Immutable return / trade sample] --> C[Method and dependence assumptions]
 C --> G[Seeded named generators]
 G --> P[Resampled paths]
 P --> A[Independent metrics]
 A --> Q[Percentiles and limitations]
```

## Reporting
```mermaid
flowchart LR
 B[BacktestResult artifacts] --> A[Defined metric calculations]
 A --> V[Tables and charts]
 B --> V
 V --> H[HTML / JSON / CSV / Parquet]
 H --> E[Artifact hashes and manifest references]
```

## Failures and future integration
Persist FAILED/CANCELLED job status with structured errors; never publish a partial
result as successful. Broker timeouts produce unknown outcome requiring reconciliation,
not blind retries. EngineAdapter permits later LEAN comparison/alternative backend;
vectorised acceleration must match reference semantics on its declared subset.
MATLAB can later supply models through an adapter, not own accounting.
Windows process boundaries do not alone sandbox hostile Python; M16 adds actual OS
restrictions and verification before arbitrary untrusted code becomes supported.

domain_model.text:
# Domain model and public contracts

All contracts below are specifications, not implemented classes. Validation errors
are typed failures, not silent data repair. Identifiers are immutable strings with
distinct RunId/StrategyId/OrderId/FillId/InstrumentId types. Immutable records carry
schema_version, event_id, event_time, available_at, run_id and per-run sequence.

| Contract | Input and output | Owner / failures |
|---|---|---|
| Clock | now(); advance(aware UTC) | engine; rejects backward time |
| DataFeed | history(instrument, end, count, capability) → immutable bars | availability checks; future access rejected |
| Strategy | initialize, on_bar, on_order_update, on_fill, on_end | no ledger writes; callback failure terminates run |
| StrategyContext | visible history, portfolio snapshot, submit(intent), cancel(id) | intent channel only; no broker handle |
| OrderIntent | instrument, side, quantity, type, limit/stop, TIF, client_intent_id | positive finite quantity; validated tick and currency |
| RiskManager | evaluate(intent, current snapshot, reservations) → accept/reject + reason | fail closed; never edits historical limits |
| Broker | submit/cancel/reconcile; immutable order events and fills | common historical/paper/live interface |
| ExecutionModel | eligible orders + next market event → proposed fills | respects timing and shared capacity |
| FillModel | order, bar, remaining capacity → quantities/reference prices | no same-decision-bar fills |
| SlippageModel | proposed fill + assumptions → adverse price/cost | constrained limit and valid positive price |
| CommissionModel | execution facts + cumulative order fees → fee delta | deterministic and independently testable |
| Portfolio | apply(fill/action/cash event) → immutable snapshot | single ledger writer; duplicate ID rejected/idempotent |
| Position | signed FIFO lots, units, cost basis, marks, stale flag | derived from events; no strategy mutation |
| BacktestEngine | manifest, capabilities, strategy factory → BacktestResult | FAILED on integrity faults |
| BacktestResult | typed tables + manifest/artifact references | no hidden mutable strategy state |
| Optimizer | IS capability, search space, objective, seed → all trials | OOS inaccessible; undefined metrics ineligible |
| WalkForwardEngine | frozen window plan → IS decisions + OOS results | overlaps/leakage rejected |
| MonteCarloEngine | sample, method, seed, path count → path metrics | records dependence assumptions and valid samples |
| MetricsEngine | BacktestResult + conventions → values + defined/status fields | undefined is null with reason, not zero |
| ExperimentRepository | create immutable manifest/artifacts; query/rerun/compare | conflict on overwrite, atomic completion |
| ReportGenerator | result + metrics → escaped HTML and exports | no execution of uploaded content |

## Lifecycles
Strategy: create → initialize → ordered callbacks → on_end → dispose. Terminal
exception prevents further intents and records failure. Warm-up invokes indicators
with visible history but suppresses order submission and performance accumulation.

Order: CREATED → SUBMITTED → ACCEPTED → PARTIALLY_FILLED → FILLED. SUBMITTED may
be REJECTED; ACCEPTED/PARTIALLY_FILLED may become CANCELLED, EXPIRED or receive a terminal
REJECTED event for the unfilled residual after a fill-time risk failure. That event
preserves all executed quantity and immutable fills; rejection never undoes executions.
Release only unfilled cash/quantity reservations on terminal rejection, cancellation
or expiry; never release resources already consumed by fills.
Terminal states cannot
receive new fills except explicitly reconciled out-of-order broker events with
validated execution time, represented as additional facts rather than rewritten events.
One order has many fills. A trade is reconstructed FIFO matched quantity, separate
from both order and fill. Reversals close old lots before opening new lots.

Job: QUEUED → RUNNING → SUCCEEDED | FAILED | CANCELLED. Run success requires all
artifacts committed; interrupted staging remains non-successful. Corrections create
a new run or compensating event referencing the original.

## Agent contracts
At M13 agents use authenticated role-scoped application APIs, each request including
actor_agent_id, issue_id, correlation_id and idempotency key for job submission.
Authentication establishes actor identity; a supplied actor string alone grants nothing.
Research submits jobs; validation reads artifacts and records challenges; risk reads
exposure and decision records; operations reconcile; reporting exports. Builder roles
use explicit development assignments, not unrestricted terminal execution privileges.
All roles must later produce one relevant interaction and evidence artifact; unsupported
role capabilities are rejected explicitly. No agent receives brokerage credentials.

backtesting_conventions.text:
# Backtesting conventions, version 0.1 accepted M0 baseline

## Time, calendar and visibility
UTC-aware timestamps internally; source exchange IANA timezone and calendar version
are retained. A bar spans [start,end); available_at is at least end plus declared
publication delay. Daily bars follow actual session closes, including half days/DST.
Strategy on_bar runs only after availability. Future end or availability requests fail.
Orders generated from a completed bar cannot fill in that same bar. At each next bar,
process effective corporate actions, eligible existing orders, fills/accounting and
close valuation before delivering the completed bar to the strategy. Same-time events
use priority: effective corporate actions, eligible existing orders, fill/risk events,
accounting updates, close marks, completed-bar callback, new intents, then DAY expiry
at session end. Ties use instrument ID then submission sequence, stored in the manifest.
Bar-model fills have an economic timestamp (open for market/gap fills; bar end for
intrabar touches whose exact time is unknown) and a separate observed_at equal to
bar availability. Callbacks and the monotonic simulation clock use observed_at, never
rewind to economic time. Full-bar volume is known retrospectively to the simulator,
not to the strategy at the open. New callback intents cannot act before observed_at.
An order submitted inside a bar is ineligible for whole-bar OHLC matching; wait for
the next full bar. Availability delay must never permit retroactive fills.

## Prices, fills and costs
Market fills at next eligible open plus adverse slippage. Buy limit: open improvement
if open <= limit, otherwise touch if low <= limit; inverse for sells. Final adverse
slippage cannot cross the limit: no fill if it would. Buy stop: open if gapped above
stop, otherwise stop on high touch; inverse for sell. Triggered stop-limit becomes
eligible as limit only on the following bar (conservative ambiguity policy). Competing
dependent exits are not supported initially; reject instead of inventing intrabar order.
Model assumptions and ambiguous bar counts are included in reports.

Per-symbol available bar quantity = floor(volume * participation_rate / quantity_step)
* quantity_step, shared across orders by FIFO acceptance sequence. Default research
participation is 1%; explicitly configurable. Zero/missing volume means no fills.
This retrospective liquidity approximation is labeled, not a claim of executable depth.
Risk is rechecked at actual proposed fill prices, with fees and reserved outstanding
commitments; an unaffordable residual is rejected, never silently financed.
DAY expires at session end; GTC persists within run; no after-hours fills by default.
Delayed publication of the final session bar: evaluate existing orders against
economically eligible session prices before applying DAY expiry to the residual.
Deliver both fill and expiry updates at observed_at; new intents from those callbacks
are eligible only for a subsequent session, never the expired session. Add a delayed
close fixture; economic eligibility is separate from observation time.

Commission configuration is required: per-unit and/or notional bps, per-order minimum,
currency rounding, and fee increments per partial fill. Cumulative charged commission
equals max(minimum, cumulative calculated fee) after first fill; later partial fills
charge only the incremental difference. Cancelled unfilled orders pay no commission.
Slippage supports none/fixed/bps/volume-share with explicit parameters; no double
counting spread already included in the model. Zero costs are allowed only with
an explicit ZERO_COST_ASSUMPTION label. Finite nonnegative inputs required.

## Accounting
Single currency per run; reject mismatched instruments. Decimal precision 34,
ROUND_HALF_EVEN ledger arithmetic from decimal strings. Execution prices quantise
adversely to tick (ceil for buys, floor for sells), then recheck positivity, limit
constraints and affordability. For tick 0.01 a raw buy of100.005 becomes100.01, not100.00.
Quantities round down to step before risk validation. Fees round to currency minor
units; fill prices and sizes obey instrument ticks/steps. Internal P&L retains Decimal
precision until export. Presentation rounding never changes ledger values.
Cash decreases by signed quantity * price + fee (buy positive, sell negative).
NAV = cash + dividend receivables + sum(signed quantity * mark). No external cash flows
inside a research run initially. FIFO lot matching; entry/exit fees allocated by matched
quantity, with rounding residual assigned to final lot so totals reconcile.
Signed short accounting is tested; cash policy blocks short exposure unless the manifest
explicitly names a research-only borrow/financing assumption. No production short claim.
At nonpositive NAV halt new risk, record insolvency and leave liquidation assumptions
explicit. Do not invent prices or usable CAGR/log returns after insolvency.

## Corporate actions and marks
Raw prices plus effective-dated split/dividend events are the primary model. Reject
total-return/adjusted prices combined with cash action credits. Split changes units,
cost per unit and pending order price/quantity consistently, preserving value. Dividend
entitlement uses pre-ex-date holding, receivable accrues ex-date and transfers to cash
on pay-date; shorts accrue a liability. Unknown action timing blocks the affected run.
Missing execution bars are not forward-filled. Last mark may carry for valuation with
stale status; stale mark blocks new risk. Final positions remain open and disclosed;
an explicit end-liquidation option must generate priced fills/costs, never erase exposure.

## Analytics
NAV returns include initial capital as baseline: r[t]=V[t]/V[t-1]-1. No cash flows in
initial model. Total return = Vlast/V0-1. CAGR uses actual elapsed days/365.25 and
requires positive starting/ending wealth, positive duration and no insolvency.
Default annual metrics use session-close returns, A=252 explicit; minute runs aggregate
to sessions rather than pretending all minute observations are independent.
Annual risk-free rate defaults explicitly to 0; periodic rf=(1+annual_rf)^(1/A)-1.
Sample volatility uses ddof=1. Sharpe=sqrt(A)*mean(r-rf)/sample_std(r-rf).
Sortino uses sqrt(mean(min(r-MAR,0)^2)) over all periods; MAR convention recorded.
Sortino numerator is sqrt(A)*mean(r-periodic_MAR). An annual MAR converts as
(1+annual_MAR)^(1/A)-1; default annual MAR=0. Denominator is the per-period downside
deviation just defined. Report null when it is zero, not an infinite ratio.
Fewer than two returns, zero denominators and missing samples produce null + reason.
Do not substitute infinity in JSON. Calmar=CAGR/positive maximum drawdown; undefined
when denominator zero. Peak drawdown=1-V/running_max(V), with duration in both elapsed
time and sessions; unrecovered episodes are censored, not counted as recovered.
NAV below zero permits drawdown >100% in signed/leverage fixtures and is flagged.

Historical VaR uses losses=-returns, linear empirical quantile, horizon one session.
ES uses quantile-integral fractional tail weighting, not a threshold mean that mishandles
ties. Tail sample count is reported; estimates with <20 observations or <5 expected
tail observations are flagged insufficient. No Gaussian assumption implied.
Win rate counts closed FIFO matched trades with positive net P&L; breakeven is separate.
Profit factor=sum(positive net P&L)/abs(sum(negative net P&L)), undefined without losses.
Turnover=sum(abs(fill notional))/mean positive sampled NAV (two-way traded-notional
convention). Gross/net leverage=sum(abs/signed market values)/NAV; undefined if NAV<=0.
MAE/MFE use observable post-entry marks, label bar-resolution bounds, no inferred paths.
Remaining M6 metrics require their own formula/edge-case fixtures before implementation.

## Benchmark, randomness and research protocols
Benchmark defaults to none; alpha/beta/information ratio are unavailable until compatible
currency, sessions and total-return convention are supplied. No fabricated benchmark.
Use explicit integer seed, named independent generators and deterministic trial/window
IDs. Same seed does not prove statistical validity. Stable sorting resolves ties.
Walk-forward IS/OOS intervals are half-open, disjoint and frozen. Warm-up uses only past
data and contributes no returns. Initial stitch policy resets positions at each OOS
window, funds it from prior OOS terminal equity and includes transition liquidation
costs using the final eligible OOS close under an explicitly scheduled end-of-window
liquidation model; intervals with no executable liquidation mark fail instead of
using future data. IS portfolio wealth is never stitched into OOS. Other carry policies
need separate manifests and fixtures. Selection cannot access OOS data.
Monte Carlo distinguishes trade/IID/block bootstrap and preserves all simulation
parameters. It quantifies model-conditional uncertainty, not guaranteed future returns.

testing_strategy.text:
# Testing and quantitative validation

Write failing tests before/alongside each implemented contract. M0 is documentation
and scaffolding: no financial production code or numeric correctness claim yet.
M1 establishes pytest, Hypothesis, ruff, mypy and automatic CI. Passing a tool invocation
is not passing its intended behaviour. Retain commands, exit statuses and outputs.

## Golden Quant suite
Use 20–50 tiny synthetic markets with manually predetermined orders, fills, fees,
cash, signed lots, realised/unrealised P&L and NAV. Initial catalogue:
1 long round trip; 2 short cover; 3 partial exit; 4 multiple entry fills; 5 reversal;
6 proportional fees; 7 order minimum across partial fills; 8 market gap; 9 buy limit;
10 sell limit; 11 stop gap; 12 deferred stop-limit; 13 shared volume; 14 cancellation;
15 expiry; 16 rejected buying power; 17 split wealth conservation; 18 dividend
receivable/pay-date; 19 missing bar; 20 stale mark; 21 complete loss; 22 negative NAV;
23 constant returns/undefined Sharpe; 24 unrecovered drawdown; 25 duplicate fill;
26 no future access; 27 symbol reuse; 28 DST/holiday; 29 OOS exclusion; 30 seeded bootstrap;
31 partial fill then residual risk rejection/reservation release; 32 adverse buy/sell
tick boundaries; 33 economic-time versus observed-time callback causality.

First independent arithmetic fixture: initial cash 1000, buy 4 at 100 with fee 1:
cash=599, holdings=4; mark=105 gives NAV=1019, unrealised gross P&L=20. Sell 2 at 110
with fee 1: cash=818, holdings=2, remaining entry fee allocation=0.5; mark=108 gives
NAV=1034. Gross realised=20, gross unrealised=16, total fees=2, net wealth change=34.
Closed quantity net P&L=20-0.5-1=18.5. The remaining entry fee belongs to open lots.
This fixture deliberately distinguishes cash fees, lot allocation and marked wealth.

Split fixture: cash=100, quantity=10, mark=50, NAV=600; 2-for-1 split results quantity=20,
mark=25, NAV=600. Independent dividend fixture starts cash=100, quantity=10, mark=50;
mark falls from50 to49 at ex-date,
receivable=10; NAV remains600 before other market moves; pay-date transfers10 to cash.
Drawdown fixture NAV=[100,120,90,108,120]: peak drawdown=25%, trough at third observation,
recovery at fifth; session-close returns=[0.2,-0.25,0.2,1/9].

Golden changes require explicit rationale and approval; never regenerate expected
economics directly from the implementation being tested. Risk, accounting and validation
owners independently sign fixtures. Unsupported scenarios are planned, not fake passes.

## Test layers
Unit: formulas, states, timestamp comparisons and failure cases. Property: conservation,
no oversell in cash policy, total fills <= order quantity, deterministic ordering and
nonnegative cash where mandated. Integration: real storage/ledger/callback chain, failed
artifact writes and replay. Differential: match simple BuyAndHold/MA rules against
LEAN or Backtrader with identical timing, fees, calendar and actions; explain every
discrepancy, do not blindly accept reference outputs. End-to-end: owner's final research
lifecycle plus unchanged strategy paper parity after M17. Performance after correctness.

Tolerance policy: exact Decimal cash/lot identities with rounding deltas separately
recorded; float analytics defaults atol=1e-12, rtol=1e-10 on ordinary unit fixtures,
metric-specific documented tolerance for ill-conditioned data. Economic artifacts
reproduce exactly where Decimal, toleranced where numerical; IDs/time excluded.

## Gate evidence
Each requirement links to contract, fixture/test, result and reviewer. Report confirmed,
partial, unverified or failed. Global done criteria include lint/type/unit/integration/
property/security/docs plus relevant performance and independent financial checks.
No unexplained skips. M0 records code checks as not applicable, not passed.
All 370 later interaction tests require actual actor/job/audit evidence; roster or
task creation alone cannot meet that requirement.

security_model.text:
# Security and authority model

Local single-owner research is the initial deployment. API binds loopback when built.
No live execution is enabled by installing the terminal. Trading 212 demo setup is
separate from forward testing; no test orders or credential ingestion in M0.

Trust boundaries: imported datasets and documents; Python strategy code; API callers;
job workers; artifact store; Paperclip agents; any later broker gateway. Validate
schemas/sizes/paths, escape HTML output, prohibit traversal, and use opaque registered
strategy identifiers rather than arbitrary paths from HTTP input.

Before M16, only owner-reviewed trusted local Python strategies are supported. A frozen
object, restricted import hook, subprocess or timeout is not a sandbox against hostile
code. Design data capability filtering now; verify denied future requests. Before
arbitrary Python support, enforce filesystem, network, process, memory and CPU controls
in a tested isolation environment. Workers must not inherit secrets or the full dataset.

Agent IDs in requests are attribution, not authentication. M13 introduces per-agent
credentials stored outside project files, scoped service operations and audit trails.
Research job submission cannot alter risk limits, broker configuration or other agents'
permissions. Risk/validation actions remain independent. The project root's shared
Windows account is not a security boundary between 370 agents; disclose this limitation.

Use OS-protected credentials for a future gateway only; never pass them to strategies,
LLM prompts, issues, fixtures or reports. Paper/live credentials and endpoints separate.
No live host fallback on demo authentication failure. Reject redirects carrying auth.
Unknown submission outcomes require reconciliation; no automatic order retry.

Resource limits: bounded worker count, per-job timeout and disk/artifact limits; request
validation; job cancellation; no infinite agent polling. Idempotency and single ledger
writer prevent duplicate fills. Unknown symbols, stale data, invalid capital and missing
risk config fail closed. Logs redact secrets and exclude authentication headers.
Dependency provenance, pinned versions and license review are required before reuse.
Do not copy reference-engine code without evaluating its licence. Legal roles produce
internal research, not legal sign-off or regulatory filings.

Threat tests by milestone: M1 invalid config/log redaction; M2 future data/path traversal;
M4 duplicate fills/risk reservations; M8 overwrite/crash recovery; M13 auth/idempotency;
M16 hostile strategy escape/resource exhaustion; M17 restart/reconnect reconciliation;
M18 endpoint isolation/kill switch; M21 dependency audit, restore and load tests.

data_model.text:
# Data and experiment model

Immutable schema-versioned records; canonical UTF-8 JSON metadata with decimal
numbers serialized as strings and UTC timestamps in ISO 8601. Analytical Parquet
tables use explicit decimal/timestamp schemas, never implicit float conversion.

| Record | Required fields and integrity |
|---|---|
| Instrument | stable instrument_id, symbol history, currency, asset class, exchange/calendar, timezone, tick/quantity step, effective intervals |
| Bar | instrument_id, start, end, available_at, OHLC, volume, frequency, source; unique instrument/frequency/start/version |
| CorporateAction | action_id, type, instrument, known_at, effective_at, ratio or amount, ex/pay dates, version |
| Universe | membership effective interval, known_at, delisting history and source |
| DatasetSnapshot | hash, schema/calendar versions, interval, source/license/entitlements, raw/adjusted/total-return flags, PIT/survivorship claims and evidence |
| OrderEvent | immutable event/order/intent IDs, sequence, status, timestamp, quantity, prices, model and risk reason |
| Fill | unique fill_id/order_id, signed side/quantity, reference/fill price, fee, slippage, timestamp, model version |
| LedgerEvent | event_id, fill/action link, cash delta, lot/quantity delta, receivable delta, currency |
| PortfolioSnapshot | time, cash, receivables, positions/marks/stale flags, NAV, exposures |
| MatchedTrade | deterministic trade_id, entry/exit fill allocations, quantity, costs, net P&L, duration |
| Metric | name, value or null, status/reason, formula/version, sampling/tolerance/conventions |
| ExperimentManifest | run ID, strategy/source hash, Git commit or explicit uncommitted marker + tree hash, engine/Python/dependency/platform versions, data snapshot, all parameters/assumptions, seed, dates, initial capital, created time |
| Artifact | run ID, relative path, media/schema, checksum, byte count, completion state |
| AgentInteraction | authenticated actor, role, issue/run IDs, timestamp, operation, outcome and evidence artifact; no raw credentials |

Data validation rejects NaN/infinity, nonpositive prices, negative volume, impossible
OHLC, duplicate/out-of-order records, unknown timezones or missing required metadata.
Complete-loss/negative-NAV fixtures are analytics-only initially; later explicit
delisting/write-off ledger events can represent zero recovery. Zero executable prices
remain invalid and are not a substitute for such events.
Missing calendar bars produce diagnostics; neither prices nor volume are silently
filled. Stable symbol IDs avoid conflating symbol reuse. Corrections create a new
snapshot. All selected rows satisfy available_at <= current time and universe known_at.

Write run artifacts to unique staging, checksum and atomically finalize. SQLite tracks
status and searchable indexes; a SUCCEEDED row is written only after durable artifact
completion. Append status events for recovery. Content-address source/data snapshots
are read-only inputs; comparison excludes generated run IDs/timestamps from economic
reproducibility checks. Never claim external vendor data PIT without evidence.

roadmap.text:
# Milestone roadmap

Owner authorised automatic continuation after passed gates on 2026-09-23. Stop on failed gates; no approval bypass. Each milestone follows PLAN → SPECIFY → TEST DESIGN → IMPLEMENT → UNIT → INTEGRATION → QUANT VALIDATION → DOCUMENT → REVIEW → GATE. Full original scope and exit gates are preserved in sources/owner-brief.txt.

- M0: PRODUCT SPECIFICATION AND ARCHITECTURAL BASELINE
- M1: PROJECT FOUNDATION AND DOMAIN MODEL
- M2: HISTORICAL DATA ENGINE
- M3: PORTFOLIO AND ACCOUNTING ENGINE
- M4: ORDER MANAGEMENT AND EXECUTION SIMULATOR
- M5: EVENT-DRIVEN BACKTEST ENGINE
- M6: PERFORMANCE AND RISK ANALYTICS
- M7: PROFESSIONAL BACKTEST REPORT
- M8: EXPERIMENT MANAGEMENT AND REPRODUCIBILITY
- M9: PARAMETER OPTIMISATION ENGINE
- M10: WALK-FORWARD OPTIMISATION
- M11: MONTE CARLO AND ROBUSTNESS ENGINE
- M12: ROBUSTNESS AND OVERFITTING TOOLKIT
- M13: TERMINAL API AND CLI
- M14: PROFESSIONAL TERMINAL UI
- M15: PERFORMANCE AND SCALABILITY
- M16: SECURITY AND STRATEGY SANDBOX

M0 deliverables: eight specification documents, seven diagrams, ADRs, public contract ownership and failure semantics, golden-test design, all-role assignment map and independent review. No financial implementation at this gate.

Each later gate requires complete applicable unit/integration/property tests, lint, types, independent economic validation, documentation and an evidence report. Agent scheduling: all370 have a role scope and post-build interaction acceptance. Activate only tasks whose prerequisite gates passed; queue others. Bound concurrency to three disjoint writers.
